title: Nutrient Requirements
content:
# Nutrient Requirements

## Learning Objectives
By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
- Identify the main nutrients required by humans
- Describe the functions of carbohydrates, proteins, and lipids
- Describe the roles of vitamins and minerals
- Explain why fibre and water are important in the diet

## Introduction

**Nutrients** are substances obtained from food that the body needs for energy, growth, repair, and maintaining health. Humans require a variety of nutrients, each with specific functions. A healthy diet provides all essential nutrients in appropriate amounts.

## Key Concepts

### Classes of Nutrients

**Seven types of nutrients:**

| Nutrient | Main function |
|----------|---------------|
| Carbohydrates | Energy |
| Proteins | Growth and repair |
| Lipids (fats/oils) | Energy, insulation, membranes |
| Vitamins | Regulate body functions |
| Minerals | Various functions |
| Fibre | Digestive health |
| Water | All body processes |

### Carbohydrates

**Function:** Main source of energy

**Types:**

| Type | Examples | Found in |
|------|----------|----------|
| Simple sugars | Glucose, fructose | Fruit, honey |
| Disaccharides | Sucrose, lactose | Table sugar, milk |
| Complex (starch) | Starch | Bread, rice, potatoes |

**In the body:**
- Broken down to glucose
- Glucose used in respiration
- Provides 17 kJ per gram
- Excess stored as glycogen or fat

**Daily requirement:** ~260g (varies with activity)

### Proteins

**Functions:**
- Growth of new cells
- Repair of damaged tissue
- Making enzymes
- Making antibodies
- Making hormones
- Can be used for energy (17 kJ/g)

**Made of:** Amino acids

| Amino acid type | Description |
|----------------|-------------|
| Essential | Must be obtained from diet |
| Non-essential | Body can synthesise |

**Sources:**

| Animal sources | Plant sources |
|---------------|---------------|
| Meat, fish | Beans, lentils |
| Eggs | Nuts, seeds |
| Dairy | Soy products |

**Daily requirement:** ~50g for adults

### Lipids (Fats and Oils)

**Functions:**
- Energy source (39 kJ/g - more than carbs)
- Energy storage
- Insulation (under skin)
- Protection of organs
- Cell membrane structure
- Absorption of fat-soluble vitamins

**Types:**

| Type | Description | Sources |
|------|-------------|--------|
| Saturated | Solid at room temp | Butter, meat fat |
| Unsaturated | Liquid at room temp | Olive oil, fish oil |
| Trans fats | Processed fats | Some margarines |

**Health implications:**
- Saturated fats: linked to heart disease
- Unsaturated fats: generally healthier
- Trans fats: should be avoided

### Vitamins

**Key vitamins:**

| Vitamin | Function | Sources | Deficiency |
|---------|----------|---------|------------|
| A | Vision, skin | Carrots, liver | Night blindness |
| B group | Energy metabolism | Whole grains, meat | Various |
| C | Immune function, collagen | Citrus fruits | Scurvy |
| D | Calcium absorption, bones | Sunlight, fish | Rickets |
| E | Antioxidant | Nuts, seeds | Rare |
| K | Blood clotting | Leafy greens | Bleeding disorders |

**Fat-soluble:** A, D, E, K (stored in body)
**Water-soluble:** B, C (not stored, need daily)

### Minerals

**Key minerals:**

| Mineral | Function | Sources | Deficiency |
|---------|----------|---------|------------|
| Calcium | Bones, teeth, muscle contraction | Dairy, leafy greens | Weak bones |
| Iron | Haemoglobin in red blood cells | Red meat, spinach | Anaemia |
| Sodium | Nerve function, fluid balance | Salt, processed foods | Muscle cramps |
| Potassium | Nerve function, heart rhythm | Bananas, potatoes | Weakness |
| Iodine | Thyroid hormones | Seafood, iodised salt | Goitre |
| Phosphorus | Bones, ATP | Meat, dairy | Weakness |
| Magnesium | Enzymes, bones | Nuts, whole grains | Muscle cramps |

### Dietary Fibre

**What is fibre?**
- Indigestible plant material
- Mainly cellulose
- Not absorbed by body

**Functions:**
- Adds bulk to food
- Helps move food through gut (peristalsis)
- Prevents constipation
- May reduce cholesterol absorption
- Helps prevent bowel cancer
- Makes you feel full

**Sources:**
- Whole grains
- Vegetables
- Fruits
- Legumes

**Daily requirement:** ~30g

### Water

**Functions:**
- Solvent for reactions
- Transport medium (blood, lymph)
- Temperature regulation (sweating)
- Hydrolysis reactions
- Fills cells (turgor in plants)

**In the body:**
- Makes up ~60% of body mass
- Lost through urine, sweat, breathing
- Must be replaced daily

**Daily requirement:** ~2 litres

### Summary Table

| Nutrient | Function | Good sources |
|----------|----------|-------------|
| Carbohydrates | Energy | Bread, rice, pasta |
| Proteins | Growth, repair | Meat, fish, beans |
| Lipids | Energy, insulation | Oils, butter, nuts |
| Vitamin C | Immune function | Citrus fruits |
| Vitamin D | Bone health | Sunlight, fish |
| Calcium | Bones, teeth | Dairy, leafy greens |
| Iron | Haemoglobin | Red meat, spinach |
| Fibre | Digestive health | Whole grains, veg |
| Water | All functions | Drinks, food |

### Energy from Nutrients

| Nutrient | Energy (kJ/g) |
|----------|---------------|
| Carbohydrates | 17 |
| Proteins | 17 |
| Lipids | 39 |
| Alcohol | 29 |
| Fibre | 0 (not digested) |

**Lipids provide more than twice the energy per gram as carbohydrates or proteins.**

## Common Exam Questions

- State the functions of named nutrients
- Identify good sources of specific nutrients
- Explain deficiency diseases
- Describe the importance of fibre in the diet

## Common Misconceptions

- **Misconception:** All fats are bad for you
- **Reality:** Unsaturated fats are essential and beneficial

- **Misconception:** Carbohydrates make you fat
- **Reality:** Excess of ANY energy source causes weight gain

- **Misconception:** Vitamins provide energy
- **Reality:** Vitamins help release energy but don't provide it

- **Misconception:** You need supplements if you eat well
- **Reality:** A balanced diet usually provides all needed nutrients

## Practice Questions

1. State the function of carbohydrates in the diet. (1 mark)

2. Name two sources of protein. (2 marks)

3. Explain why fibre is important in the diet, even though it provides no energy. (3 marks)

4. Describe the functions of lipids in the body. (4 marks)

5. Explain the difference between vitamins and minerals. Give one example of each. (4 marks)

6. A person's diet is lacking in iron and vitamin D. Describe the deficiency diseases that might result and explain why these nutrients are needed. (6 marks)

## Key Terms Glossary

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| Nutrient | Substance needed for body function |
| Carbohydrate | Nutrient providing main energy source |
| Protein | Nutrient for growth and repair |
| Lipid | Fat or oil; high-energy storage |
| Vitamin | Organic compound needed in small amounts |
| Mineral | Inorganic element needed for health |
| Fibre | Indigestible plant material |
| Deficiency disease | Disease caused by lack of a nutrient |
| Essential amino acid | Amino acid that must come from diet |

## Summary

- Seven nutrient types: carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, vitamins, minerals, fibre, water
- Carbohydrates provide main energy source (17 kJ/g)
- Proteins needed for growth and repair
- Lipids store energy (39 kJ/g) and insulate
- Vitamins and minerals needed in small amounts for specific functions
- Fibre aids digestion and prevents constipation
- Water is essential for all body processes
- Deficiency diseases result from lack of specific nutrients
